newsitem.title: GERMANY: Global vegoil stocks seen falling in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Global vegoil stocks seen falling in first quarter.

text.p: Stocks of six major vegetable oils should fall to 5.12 million tonnes on April 1, from 6.14 million on January 1, independent newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.
The estimate was given on the basis of stocks in seven major exporting and 10 major importing countries plus Rotterdam bonded warehouses.
It included soyoil, palm oil, sun oil, rape oil, palmkernel oil and coconut oil.
Oil World said stocks had already fallen in Oct/Dec -- which was seasonally untypical -- because of the lower oil content of the U.S. crop as well as lower rapeseed crushings.
The first quarter decline would be most strongly felt in Indonesia, Malaysia, Argentina, Brazil, China and some others where demand was strong.
Chinese import demand was buoyant, which would mean further world stocks drawdowns in April/Sept.
Oil World estimated Chinese imports of 17 oils and fats, mostly palm oil and soyoil, in the full 1996/97 season at 4.2 million tonnes, up by 900,000 tonnes from 1995/96.
Indian buyers were seen taking more sun oil from the world market but shunning expensive palm oil after some purchases.
